Photograph: Luke Hales/Getty Images for WTA WTA Finals Svitolina stays in WTA Finals hunt after remarkable fightback sees off Muchova
 Ukrainian wins 3-6, 6-2, 6-2 after eight-minute timeout
 Andreeva beats Sabalenka 6-4, 6-0 to top Group B
 Press Association Wed 11 Nov 2026 19.23 EST First published on Wed 11 Nov 2026 18.26 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Elina Svitolina staged a remarkable comeback to beat Karolina Muchova and remain in the hunt for the WTA Finals title.
 The Ukrainian appeared to be on her way out of Indian Wells when she was a set down and required an eight-minute medical timeout. But she recovered to win 3-6, 6-2, 6-2 and stay in with a chance of reaching the semi-finals.
 Hot mics, Andreeva ‘diva’ drama and a stopgap finale at Indian Wells bail out the WTA | Tumaini Carayol Read more Svitolina, who was demolished 6-4, 6-0 by Mirra Andreeva in her opening round-robin match, told Sky Sports: “It was not an easy task to do.
 “I was pretty angry at myself after the first match and after the first set also. Things didn’t go my way, so I tried to direct this anger towards the ball and found my game in the end.
 “I think the level was back in the third set. I just tried to give it all in this match because I know I would be eliminated if I lost. So I just tried to really release all this energy and find these openings against Karolina. She’s such a tough opponent.
 “It’s the last tournament of the season, so I just have to really put my head down and deal with all the small injuries.
 “I mean, it’s normal that everyone is tired. Everyone is struggling with something here and there. I will just try to do my best, have an ice bath and try to heal as much as possible in the next 48 hours.”
 View image in fullscreen Mirra Andreeva (left) embraces Aryna Sabalenka at the net after winning their group-stage match. Photograph: Daniel Cole/Reuters Svitolina faces a straight shootout with Aryna Sabalenka for second place in the group. Andreeva, the French Open champion, secured her place in the last four after coming from 4-1 down in the first set to beat Sabalenka 6-4, 6-0.
 Andreeva tops Group B with Sabalenka second and Svitolina third.
